observation: ONE SENTENCE in that row's `factor_2_basis` was false when written. It reads that an open PR 'appears to be adding exactly this truncated-listing family as T1C; it is NOT merged, and an unmerged template is not an allowlist entry.' T1C had merged at 08:00:40Z — 23 minutes BEFORE that capture was stamped 08:24:01Z. Confirmed from git by the Architect on #409, not from any report.
what_still_stands: The VERDICT is unchanged and correct. It rests on `factor_1: unverifiable`, and either factor being unverifiable routes ANOMALOUS regardless of the other — so Factor 2 was never load-bearing for this classification. Every machine-read field in that row is correct: classification anomalous, factor_1 unverifiable, channel unknown, stated_cause_false false. `template_id: null` is UNVERIFIABLE rather than known-false: the recorded verbatim has its listing elided by the capturing agent, so nothing can be matched against it (#408). No measurement reads the field that is wrong.
why_this_row_exists_rather_than_an_edit: #409 ruled option C: merged rows stay immutable and the append-only guard is unchanged. MUTATION IN PLACE IS LOSS THAT PRESERVES THE COUNT — rewriting a row destroys the prior row exactly as deletion does, and does it invisibly, because every count-based check still passes. The decisive precedent is #387, whose central finding existed ONLY because four rows recorded classifications that were wrong; had each been corrected in place, each individually defensible, that finding would have been permanently undiscoverable. The signal was the DELTA between what was concluded and what was correct, and in-place correction erases deltas by construction.
why_no_verbatim: DELIBERATE AND LOAD-BEARING, not an omission. With no `verbatim` the head-matcher cannot match this row, so it never enters any template's `live` denominator and cannot double-count against the row it supersedes. That is what makes an appended observation cheaper than a correction, and it leaves the `corpus_matches` unit question (#397 part 1) untouched. check-concealment-captures REFUSES a supersedes row carrying `verbatim`, so this is enforced rather than merely intended.
what_this_does_NOT_supersede: THE EVIDENCE. That row is the ONLY instance of allowlist staleness in 101 rows, and its value is precisely that it records a confidently-wrong Factor 2 produced by an agent doing exactly what it was told. This row corrects ONE SENTENCE; it does not retire the observation, and a reader who treats the superseded row as withdrawn has lost the finding.
the_defect_underneath: The classifier's allowlist is whatever is in the agent's worktree, and nothing requires it to be current. Checked rather than assumed: #410 shipped `templates_revision`, which records WHICH allowlist blob was read — making staleness DETECTABLE, not preventing it. Its own README says 'Nothing about reading the file changes... You now also record which one you read', and lists fetching from origin/main and requiring a freshness check as 'two repairs that were considered and rejected — do not re-propose them'. So the cause remains live BY DECISION rather than by oversight. Note this row's subject predates `templates_revision` and carries none; per #410 that absence means 'predates the field', not 'unverifiable'.
supersedes_field_note: `supersedes` carries the PATH relative to .operum/audit/, because that is what the only consumer reads — check-concealment-captures compares it against `file.rel` with that prefix stripped. #409's ruling wrote the identifier as the timestamp `2026-08-26T08:24:01Z`; that is preserved in `supersedes_ts` rather than dropped, since a timestamp in `supersedes` would be a value the validator cannot match. Flagged to PM rather than silently chosen.
action_taken: No file was modified. The superseded row, the append-only guard and the frozen log are all untouched.
